english.heading: Small Livestock Integration
body: Small livestock integration turns chickens, ducks, and bees into working parts of the farm.
Learn how animals can control pests, build fertility, support pollination, and return value to the soil.
Use the system you already have: food, manure, flowers, grazing, and careful movement across the land.

heading.text: Ku Hlanganisa Swifuwo Leswitsongo
heading.backTranslation: Integrating Small Livestock

body.text: Ku hlanganisa swifuwo leswitsongo swi endla leswaku tihuku (chickens), masekwa (ducks) na tinyoxi (bees) swi va swiphemu leswi tirhaka swa purasi.
body.backTranslation: Integrating small livestock makes chickens, ducks and bees become working parts of the farm.

body.text: Dyondza ndlela leyi swifuwo swi nga lawulaka pests, swi antswisaka soil fertility, swi pfunaka pollination ni ku tlherisela nkoka emisaveni.
body.backTranslation: Learn the way in which livestock can/may control pests, improve soil fertility, help pollination and give back importance/value to the earth.

body.text: Tirhisa sisiteme leyi se u nga na yona: swakudya, manyoro, swiluva, ku dyisa ni ku fambisa swifuwo hi vukheta emisaveni.
body.backTranslation: Use the system that you already have: feed, manure, flowers, grazing and moving livestock carefully on the soil.

english.heading: Why This Matters
body: Small livestock can do work beyond producing meat, eggs, or honey.
Chickens eat some insects and weed seeds. Their manure can become compost.
Ducks scratch less than chickens, but can still damage plants.
Bees and other pollinators help many crops. Each animal still needs suitable food, water, shelter and care.

heading.text: Ha Yini Leswi Swi Ni Nkoka
heading.backTranslation: Why This Matters

body.text: Swifuwo leswitsongo swi nga endla mintirho yo tala handle ka ku humesa nyama, matandza kumbe vulombe.
body.backTranslation: Small livestock can do many jobs apart from producing meat, eggs or honey.

body.text: Tihuku (chickens) ti dya switsotswana swin'wana ni mbewu ya swimila leswi nga laveki (weed seeds). Manyoro ya tona ma nga va compost.
body.backTranslation: Chickens eat some small insects and seed of unwanted plants (weed seeds). Their manure can become compost.

body.text: Masekwa (ducks) a ma celi misava ngopfu kukota tihuku (chickens), kambe ma nga ha onha swimila.
body.backTranslation: Ducks (ducks) do not dig the soil as much as chickens (chickens), but they may still damage plants.

body.text: Tinyoxi (bees) ni pollinators tin'wana ti pfuna swibyariwa swo tala. Xifuwo xin'wana ni xin'wana xi ha lava swakudya leswi faneleke, mati, ndhawu yo tumbela ni vuhlayisi.
body.backTranslation: Bees (bees) and other pollinators help many crops. Each animal still needs suitable food, water, a place for hiding and care.

english.heading: Learning Outcomes
body: By the end of this module, you will understand how chickens, ducks, bees, and guinea fowl fit into a working system.
You will know when chickens help a bed, and when their scratching can cause damage.
You will understand pollination, hive placement, and how livestock move nutrients around a farm.

heading.text: Leswi U Nga Ta Dyondza Swona
heading.backTranslation: What You Will Learn

body.text: Loko module leyi yi hela, u ta twisisa ndlela leyi tihuku (chickens), masekwa (ducks), tinyoxi (bees) na guinea fowl swi tirhaka ha yona eka sisiteme leyi tirhaka.
body.backTranslation: When this module ends, you will understand how chickens, ducks, bees and guinea fowl work in a working system.

body.text: U ta tiva loko tihuku (chickens) ti pfuna bedi ya ku byala (garden bed), ni loko ku cela ka tona ku nga onha.
body.backTranslation: You will know when chickens help a planting bed (garden bed), and when their scratching can damage.

body.text: U ta twisisa pollination, ndhawu yo veka hive, ni ndlela leyi swifuwo swi fambisaka swakudya swa swimilana (nutrients) ha yona eka purasi.
body.backTranslation: You will understand pollination, a place to put a hive, and the way in which livestock move food of plants (nutrients) by it on the farm.

english.heading: Watch: Hens Foraging After Harvest
body: Watch the hens peck at the ground among dry plant remains.
Chickens may eat some insects and weed seeds. They still need balanced feed, clean water and shelter.
Keep them away from seedlings and food ready to harvest.

heading.text: Languta: Tihuku Ti Dya Endzhaku ka Ntshovelo
heading.backTranslation: Look: Chickens Eat After Harvest

body.text: Languta tihuku (hens) ti lava swakudya emisaveni exikarhi ka masalela ya swimilana leswi omeke.
body.backTranslation: Look at hens looking for food on the soil among dry plant remains.

body.text: Tihuku (chickens) ti nga dya switsotswana swin'wana ni mbewu ya swimila leswi nga laveki (weed seeds). Ti ha lava swakudya leswi ringanisiweke, mati lama tengeke ni ndhawu yo tumbela.
body.backTranslation: Chickens can eat some small insects and seed of unwanted plants (weed seeds). They still need balanced feed, clean water and a place to hide.

body.text: Ti hlayise ekule ni swimilana leswintshwa (seedlings) ni swakudya leswi lunghekeke ku tshoveriwa.
body.backTranslation: Keep them away from young plants (seedlings) and food that is ready to be harvested.

english.heading: Chickens Turn Scratching Into Useful Work
body: Chickens can help an empty bed after harvest.
They scratch through plant remains and eat some insects and weed seeds.
Their manure and bedding can be composted and returned to the soil.
Foraging does not replace a balanced diet, clean water, shelter or daily care.

heading.text: Ku Cela ka Tihuku Ku Va Ntirho wa Nkoka
heading.backTranslation: Scratching of Chickens Becomes Important Work

body.text: Tihuku (chickens) ti nga pfuna bedi ya ku byala leyi nga riki na nchumu endzhaku ka ku tshovela.
body.backTranslation: Chickens can help an empty planting bed after harvesting.

body.text: Ti cela hi le ndzeni ka masalela ya swimilana ni ku dya switsotswana swin'wana ni mbewu ya swimila leswi nga laveki (weed seeds).
body.backTranslation: They scratch inside the plant remains and eat some small insects and seed of unwanted plants (weed seeds).

body.text: Manyoro ya tona ni swo andlala (bedding) swi nga endliwa compost kutani swi tlheriseriwa emisaveni.
body.backTranslation: Their manure and bedding can be made into compost and returned to the soil.

body.text: Ku tilavela swakudya ka tona a ku vuyeteli swakudya leswi ringanisiweke, mati lama tengeke, ndhawu yo tumbela kumbe vuhlayisi bya siku na siku.
body.backTranslation: Their feeding for themselves does not replace balanced food, clean water, a place to hide or daily care.

english.heading: Use Chickens at the Right Time
body: Use chickens in an empty bed after harvest.
Keep them away from seedlings and crops being harvested for food.
Fresh manure can carry germs. Ask an extension adviser how to manage manure safely before the next crop.
Move the birds before they damage the ground.

heading.text: Tirhisa Tihuku Hi Nkarhi Lowu Faneleke
heading.backTranslation: Use Chickens at the Right Time

body.text: Tirhisa tihuku (chickens) eka bedi ya ku byala leyi nga riki na nchumu endzhaku ka ku tshovela.
body.backTranslation: Use chickens in an empty planting bed after harvesting.

body.text: Ti hlayise ekule ni swimilana leswintshwa (seedlings) ni swibyariwa leswi tshoveriwaka ku va swakudya.
body.backTranslation: Keep them away from young plants (seedlings) and crops that are harvested to be food.

body.text: Manyoro lamantshwa ma nga rhwala germs. Vutisa extension adviser ndlela yo lawula manyoro hi ku hlayiseka ku nga si va swibyariwa leswi landzelaka.
body.backTranslation: Fresh manure may carry germs. Ask an extension adviser the way to manage manure safely before the next crops.

body.text: Fambisa swinyenyana ku nga si va swi onha misava.
body.backTranslation: Move the birds before they damage the soil.

english.heading: Ducks Suit Established Understorey
body: Ducks eat slugs and snails without the heavy scratching of chickens.
They may suit an established food forest understorey.
They can still eat or trample plants and make wet ground muddy. Watch the birds and move them when needed.
Provide clean water and suitable feed; foraging alone may not be enough.

heading.text: Masekwa ma Fambisana na Understorey leyi Tiyeke
heading.backTranslation: Ducks Go Together with a Strong Understorey

body.text: Masekwa (ducks) ma dya slugs na snails, kambe a ma cela-celi misava hi matimba ku fana na tihuku.
body.backTranslation: Ducks eat slugs and snails, but they do not scratch the soil hard like chickens.

body.text: Ma nga fambisana ni understorey ya food forest leyi tiyeke.
body.backTranslation: They can go together with an understorey of a food forest that is strong.

body.text: Ma nga ha dya kumbe ku kandziya swimila ni ku endla misava leyi tele mati yi va ni ndzhope. Languta swinyenyana kutani u swi fambisa loko swi laveka.
body.backTranslation: They may eat or trample plants and make soil that has a lot of water muddy. Watch the birds and move them when needed.

body.text: Nyika mati lama tengeke ni swakudya leswi faneleke; ku tilavela swakudya ntsena swi nga ha nga ringani.
body.backTranslation: Give clean water and suitable food; feeding for themselves alone may not be balanced.

english.heading: Rotate the Tractor Across the Plot
body: A chicken tractor is a moveable, floorless pen.
Move it before the ground becomes bare, muddy or heavily covered with manure.
The right time depends on the birds, soil and weather. Let the ground recover between visits.
There is no single number of chickens that guarantees enough fertility for every plot.

heading.text: Fambisa Chicken Tractor eka Swiphemu Hinkwaswo
heading.backTranslation: Move the Chicken Tractor to All Parts

body.text: Chicken tractor i xivaka xa tihuku (chickens) lexi fambisekaka, lexi nga riki na hansi.
body.backTranslation: A chicken tractor is a movable house of chickens that has no floor.

body.text: Yi fambise ku nga si va misava yi hava swimilana, yi va ni ndzhope kumbe yi funengeteriwe swinene hi manyoro.
body.backTranslation: Move it before the soil gets bare of plants, becomes muddy or is covered too much with manure.

body.text: Nkarhi lowu faneleke wu titshege hi swinyenyana, misava ni xiyimo xa moya. Pfumelela misava yi tlhela yi antswa exikarhi ka ku endzela.
body.backTranslation: The right timing depends on the birds, the soil and the state of the weather. Allow the soil to improve again between visits.

body.text: A ku na nhlayo yin'we ya tihuku (chickens) leyi tiyisaka leswaku ku ta va ni fertility leyi ringaneke eka xiphemu xin'wana ni xin'wana xa masimu.
body.backTranslation: There is no single number of chickens that guarantees that there will be sufficient fertility in every part of the fields.

english.heading: Watch: A Bee Moves Between Two Blossoms
body: Watch one bee move from one blossom to another.
Bees can carry pollen as they visit flowers.

heading.text: Languta: Nyoxi Yi Famba Eka Swiluva Swimbirhi
heading.backTranslation: Look: A Bee Goes Between Two Flowers

body.text: Languta nyoxi (bee) yin'we yi suka eka xiluva yi ya eka xin'wana.
body.backTranslation: Look at one bee leaving a flower and going to another.

body.text: Tinyoxi (bees) ti nga rhwala pollen loko ti endzela swiluva.
body.backTranslation: Bees (bees) can/may carry pollen when they visit flowers.

english.heading: Bees Help Pollinate Many Crops
body: Honeybees and other insects carry pollen between flowers.
This helps many fruit and vegetable crops, including avocado. Different crops and varieties have different pollination needs.
A hive does not guarantee higher yields everywhere. Weather, water, plant health and other pollinators also matter.

heading.text: Tinyoxi Ti Pfuna Pollination ya Swibyariwa Swo Tala
heading.backTranslation: Bees Help Pollination of Many Crops

body.text: Tinyoxi ta vulombe (honeybees) ni switsotswana swin'wana swi rhwala pollen exikarhi ka swiluva.
body.backTranslation: Bees of honey (honeybees) and other insects carry pollen between flowers.

body.text: Leswi swi pfuna swibyariwa swo tala swa mihandzu ni swa miroho, ku katsa avocado. Swibyariwa ni mixaka (varieties) leswi hambaneke swi ni swilaveko leswi hambaneke swa pollination.
body.backTranslation: These help many crops of fruits and of vegetables, including avocado. Crops and varieties (varieties) that differ have requirements that differ, of pollination.

body.text: Hive a yi tiyisekisi leswaku vuyelo (yields) byi ta tlakuka ndhawu hinkwayo. Xiyimo xa moya (weather), mati, rihanyo ra swimilana ni pollinators tin'wana na swona swi na nkoka.
body.backTranslation: A hive does not guarantee that the yields (yields) will rise everywhere. The condition of the air (weather), water, the health of plants and other pollinators, they too have importance.

english.heading: South Africa’s Native Honeybees
body: South Africa has two native honeybee subspecies.
The Cape honeybee is found in the Western Cape and parts of the Eastern Cape. The African honeybee is native to central and most of southern Africa.
These broad natural ranges are not a guide for moving bees. The Department's control measures set a demarcation line for bee movement. Check current rules before moving bees or hives.

heading.text: Tinyoxi ta Vulombe ta Ntumbuluko eAfrika-Dzonga
heading.backTranslation: Natural (Native) Honeybees in South Africa

body.text: Afrika-Dzonga ri ni subspecies timbirhi ta tinyoxi ta vulombe (honeybee) ta ntumbuluko.
body.backTranslation: South Africa has two native subspecies of honeybees.

body.text: Cape honeybee yi kumeka eWestern Cape ni swiphemu swin'wana swa Eastern Cape. African honeybee yi ta ntumbuluko eka Afrika ya le xikarhi ni swo tala swa le dzongeni ka Afrika.
body.backTranslation: The Cape honeybee is found in the Western Cape and some parts of the Eastern Cape. The African honeybee is native in central Africa and most of the south of Africa.

body.text: Ndhawu leyi leyikulu ya ntumbuluko a hi nkongomiso wa ku fambisa tinyoxi (bees). Milawu ya ku lawula (control measures) ya Ndzawulo (Department) yi vekile demarcation line ya ku fambisa tinyoxi. Kambisisa milawu ya sweswi ku nga si fambisiwa tinyoxi kumbe tihive.
body.backTranslation: The big natural area is not a guide for moving bees (bees). The control measures (control measures) of the Department (Department) set a demarcation line for moving bees. Check the current rules before bees or hives are moved.

english.heading: Place the Hive With Care
body: Learn from an experienced local beekeeper before getting a hive.
Keep hives away from busy paths, homes and places where children play.
Morning sun can help, but a safe location comes first.
Plan how people and animals will move around the site.

heading.text: Veka Hive Hi Ku Tivonela
heading.backTranslation: Put the Hive With Care

body.text: Dyondza eka mufuwi wa tinyoxi (bees) wa ndhawu la nga ni ntokoto ku nga si va u kuma hive.
body.backTranslation: Learn from an experienced local beekeeper before you get a hive.

body.text: Hlayisa tihive ekule ni tindlela leti nga ni vanhu vo tala, tindlu ni ndhawu leyi vana va tlangaka eka yona.
body.backTranslation: Keep hives away from paths that have many people, houses and the place where children play.

body.text: Dyambu ra mixo ri nga pfuna, kambe ndhawu leyi hlayisekeke yi rhanga.
body.backTranslation: Morning sun can help, but a safe place comes first.

body.text: Pulana ndlela leyi vanhu ni swifuwo swi nga ta fambafamba ha yona ku rhendzela ndhawu.
body.backTranslation: Plan the way that people and livestock will walk around the area.

english.heading: Strong Colonies Need Care and Flowers
body: Provide flowering plants through the seasons and avoid exposing bees to pesticides.
Active bees do not prove that the farm is free of chemicals or disease.

Registration is required for activities defined by the national honey-bee control measures. These include keeping managed hives for bee products, queen rearing, commercial pollination, and removing, eradicating or relocating colonies. Check with the Department if you are unsure whether your activity is covered.
If a colony swarms repeatedly, ask a trained beekeeper to inspect it. Crowding is one possible cause, not a diagnosis.

heading.text: Tinyoxi Leti Tiyeke Ti Lava Vuhlayisi ni Swiluva
heading.backTranslation: Strong Bees Need Care and Flowers

body.text: Nyika swimilana leswi nga ni swiluva eka tinguva hinkwato, u papalata ku paluxa tinyoxi (bees) eka pesticides.
body.backTranslation: Give plants that have flowers at all times, and avoid exposing bees to pesticides.

body.text: Tinyoxi (bees) leti hanyaka ni ku tirha a ti kombisi leswaku purasi a yi na tikhemikhali kumbe vuvabyi.
body.backTranslation: Bees that live and work do not show that the farm has no chemicals or disease.

body.text: Ku tsarisa ku laveka eka mintirho leyi vekiweke hi national honey-bee control measures. Yi katsa ku hlayisa tihive leti lawuriwaka ku kuma swilo leswi humaka eka tinyoxi (bees), queen rearing, commercial pollination, ni ku susa, ku herisa kumbe ku hundzisa colony. Vutisa Ndzawulo loko u nga tiyiseki leswaku ntirho wa wena wu katsekile.
body.backTranslation: Registering is required for the activities that are designated by national honey-bee control measures. It includes keeping hives that are controlled in order to get things that come from bees (bees), queen rearing, commercial pollination, and removing, ending/destroying or transferring a colony. Ask the Division if you are not sure that your activity is included.

body.text: Loko ntlawa wa tinyoxi (bees) wu endla swarm hi ku phindha-phindha, kombela mufuwi wa tinyoxi la leteriweke leswaku a wu kambela. Ku tala ka tinyoxi ehivini i xin'wana xa swivangelo leswi nga endlekaka, a hi ku tiva leswaku xiphiqo i yini.
body.backTranslation: If a group of bees (bees) makes a swarm repeatedly, ask a keeper of bees who has been [leteriweke - unrecognised] that he/she check it. Many bees in the hive is one of the causes that can happen; it is not knowing what the problem is.

english.heading: Nutrients Moving Through the Farm
body: Some nutrients move from plants to animals. Bought feed also brings nutrients into the farm. Some nutrients may return to the growing area through compost made from manure. Food and other products carry nutrients away.

heading.text: Nutrients Leti Fambaka eka Purasi
heading.backTranslation: Nutrients that Move on the Farm

body.text: Nutrients tin'wana ti famba ti suka eka swimilana ti ya eka swifuwo. Swakudya swa swifuwo leswi xaviweke na swona swi tisa nutrients eka purasi. Nutrients tin'wana ti nga tlhela ti tlhelela endhawini yo mila hi compost leyi endliweke hi manyoro. Swakudya ni swin'wana leswi humesiweke swi rhwala nutrients swi ti suse.
body.backTranslation: Some nutrients move from plants to livestock. Livestock feed that is bought also brings nutrients to the farm. Some nutrients may return to the growing place through compost that is made from manure. Feed and other things that are taken out carry nutrients and take them away.

english.heading: Some Nutrients Return; Others Enter and Leave
body: Animals can return some nutrients through compost made from manure. Fresh manure can carry harmful germs. Compost manure fully before using it around food crops.
Chickens eat suitable farm produce and insects.
Bought feed brings nutrients into the farm. Food sold or taken home and other products carry nutrients away. Keep track of feed bought in and food sold or taken home.
Scraps alone may not meet the animals’ needs.

heading.text: Tin'wana Ti Tlhela; Tin'wana Ti Nghena Ti Huma
heading.backTranslation: Some Return; Some Go In and Out

body.text: Swifuwo swi nga tlherisa nutrients tin'wana hi compost leyi endliweke hi manyoro. Manyoro lamantshwa ma nga rhwala germs leti tisaka vuvabyi. Endla manyoro compost hi ku helela ku nga si va u ma tirhisa ekusuhi ni swibyariwa swa swakudya.
body.backTranslation: Livestock may return some nutrients (nutrients) through compost that is made from manure. Fresh manure may carry germs that bring disease. Make manure into compost completely before you use it near food crops.

body.text: Tihuku (chickens) ti dya swakudya swa le purasi leswi faneleke ni switsotswana.
body.backTranslation: Chickens eat suitable food of the farm and small insects.

body.text: Swakudya swa swifuwo leswi xaviweke swi tisa nutrients eka purasi. Swakudya leswi xavisiweke kumbe leswi rhwariweke ku ya ekaya ni swin'wana swi rhwala nutrients swi ti suse. Tsala swakudya swa swifuwo leswi xaviweke ni swakudya leswi xavisiweke kumbe leswi rhwariweke ku ya ekaya.
body.backTranslation: Bought livestock feed brings nutrients to the farm. Food that is sold or carried home and other things carry nutrients and remove them. Write down the bought livestock feed and the food that is sold or carried home.

body.text: Masalela ya swakudya ntsena ma nga ha nga ringanisi swilaveko swa swifuwo.
body.backTranslation: Remains of food alone may not make the needs of livestock balanced/equal.

english.heading: Guinea Fowl Forage, but Health Checks Still Matter
body: Guinea fowl forage for insects and may eat ticks.
Do not rely on them to protect people or livestock from ticks or tick-borne disease.
Keep checking animals and follow a local animal-health plan.
Foraging birds are one part of the farm, not a replacement for health care.

heading.text: Guinea Fowl: Ku Kambela Rihanyo Ku Ha Ni Nkoka
heading.backTranslation: Guinea Fowl: Checking Health Is Still Important

body.text: Guinea fowl ti lava switsotswana, ti nga ha dya ticks.
body.backTranslation: Guinea fowl need small insects, they may eat ticks.

body.text: U nga titshegi hi tona ku sirhelela vanhu kumbe swifuwo eka ticks kumbe vuvabyi lebyi rhwariwaka hi ticks.
body.backTranslation: Do not rely on them to protect people or livestock from ticks or disease carried by ticks.

body.text: Ya emahlweni ku kambela swifuwo, u landzela pulani ya rihanyo ra swifuwo (animal-health plan) ya ndhawu.
body.backTranslation: Go on checking the livestock, following the animal health plan (animal-health plan) of the area.

body.text: Swinyenyana leswi tilavelaka swakudya i xiphemu xin'we xa purasi, a hi leswi vuyetelaka vuhlayisi bya rihanyo.
body.backTranslation: Birds that feed themselves are one part of the farm, they are not what replaces health care.

english.heading: Ask Three Questions for Every Animal
body: For each animal, ask what it can eat here.
Ask what useful things it produces.
Then ask what else it needs. Include water, suitable feed, shelter, fencing and daily care.
Some needs may require bought inputs. Plan for them before bringing animals onto the land.

heading.text: Swivutiso Swinharhu: Xifuwo Xin'wana Ni Xin'wana
heading.backTranslation: Three Questions: Each Animal

body.text: Eka xifuwo xin'wana ni xin'wana, vutisa leswaku xi nga dya yini laha.
body.backTranslation: For each animal, ask what it can eat here.

body.text: Vutisa leswaku xi humesa yini ya nkoka.
body.backTranslation: Ask what important thing it produces.

body.text: Kutani vutisa leswaku xi lava yini swin'wana. Katsa mati, swakudya leswi faneleke, ndhawu yo tumbela, fencing ni vuhlayisi bya siku na siku.
body.backTranslation: Then ask what else it needs. Include water, suitable feed, a place to hide, fencing and daily care.

body.text: Swilaveko swin'wana swi nga lava swilo leswi xaviweke. Endla pulani ya swona ku nga si tisiwa swifuwo emisaveni.
body.backTranslation: Some needs may require things that are bought. Make a plan for them before livestock are brought onto the ground.

english.heading: Grazing and Goat Worm Control
body: Chickens following goats are not a proven replacement for goat worm control.
Grazing management can help, but goats still need health checks.
Work with a veterinary or animal-health adviser on a parasite plan for your herd.
Do not stop treatment because chickens have visited the grazing camp.

heading.text: Ku Dyisa ni Ku Lawula Worms eka Timbuti (goats)
heading.backTranslation: Grazing and Controlling Worms in Goats

body.text: Ku va tihuku (chickens) ti landzela timbuti (goats) a hi ndlela leyi tiyisisiweke ematshan'wini ya ku lawula worms ta le ndzeni (internal parasitic worms) eka timbuti.
body.backTranslation: Having chickens follow goats is not a proven way in place of controlling internal parasitic worms in goats.

body.text: Ku lawula ndhawu yo dyisa swi nga pfuna, kambe timbuti (goats) ti ha lava ku kamberiwa rihanyo.
body.backTranslation: Controlling the grazing place can help, but goats still need to be checked for health.

body.text: Tirhisana ni dokodela wa swifuwo kumbe mupfuni wa rihanyo ra swifuwo eka pulani ya parasite ya ntlhambi wa wena wa timbuti (goats).
body.backTranslation: Work together with a veterinarian or animal-health helper on a parasite plan for your herd of goats.

body.text: U nga tshiki ku nyika mirhi (treatment) hikuva tihuku (chickens) ti endzerile ekampeni ya ku dyisa (grazing camp).
body.backTranslation: Do not stop giving medicine (treatment) because chickens have visited the grazing camp.

english.heading: Field Assignment: Draw Where Resources Go
body: Walk your smallholding and choose an area where livestock could support another part of the system.
Record what food, scraps, pests, surplus produce, manure, or flowering resources are already present.
Then note what each animal could produce, and what it would need from the farm.
Draw one useful link between livestock and the rest of your farm. Show what comes in and what leaves.

heading.text: Ntirho wa Masimu: Dirowa Laha Swilo Swi Ya Kona
heading.backTranslation: Fieldwork: Draw Where Things Go

body.text: Famba eka purasi ya wena yitsongo u hlawula ndhawu leyi swifuwo swi nga seketelaka xiphemu xin'wana xa sisiteme eka yona.
body.backTranslation: Walk on your small farm and choose a place where livestock can support one part of the system.

body.text: Tsala leswi nga kona sweswi: swakudya, masalela ya swakudya, pests, swibyariwa leswi tlulaka, manyoro kumbe swilo swa swiluva.
body.backTranslation: Write what is there now: feed, food remains, pests, crops that are surplus, manure or things of flowers.

body.text: Kutani tsala leswi xifuwo xin'wana ni xin'wana xi nga swi humesaka, ni leswi xi nga ta swi lava eka purasi.
body.backTranslation: Then write what each animal can produce, and what it will need from the farm.

body.text: Dirowa ku hlanganisa kun'we ka nkoka exikarhi ka swifuwo ni xiphemu lexi saleke xa purasi ya wena. Kombisa leswi nghenaka ni leswi humaka.
body.backTranslation: Draw the important joining together between livestock and the remaining part of your farm. Show what goes in and what comes out.

english.heading: Field Action: Put One Link to Work
body: Choose one safe action from this module.
Plan how chickens could use an empty bed after harvest, ask a beekeeper about a safe hive position, or check your animals’ daily needs.
Record the food, water, shelter and care that the action requires.
Start with the resources and help you can reliably provide.

heading.text: Ntirho wa Masimu: Tirhisa Ku Hlanganisa Kun'we
heading.backTranslation: Fieldwork: Use the Joining Together

body.text: Hlawula ntirho wun'we lowu hlayisekeke eka module leyi.
body.backTranslation: Choose one safe task in this module.

body.text: Pulana ndlela leyi tihuku (chickens) ti nga tirhisaka bedi ya ku byala leyi nga riki na nchumu ha yona endzhaku ka ku tshovela, vutisa mufuwi wa tinyoxi (bees) hi ndhawu leyi hlayisekeke ya hive, kumbe kambela swilaveko swa siku na siku swa swifuwo swa wena.
body.backTranslation: Plan how chickens can use an empty planting bed after harvesting, ask a beekeeper about a safe place for a hive, or check the daily needs of your livestock.

body.text: Tsala swakudya, mati, ndhawu yo tumbela ni vuhlayisi leswi ntirho lowu wu swi lavaka.
body.backTranslation: Write the feed, water, place to hide and care that this task needs.

body.text: Sungula hi swilo ni mpfuno leswi u nga swi nyikaka minkarhi hinkwayo.
body.backTranslation: Start with the things and help that you can give at all times.
